title: Device-local fabric map (PROPOSAL — consumer owns the final schema)
description: PROPOSAL ONLY. docs/workflow.md puts the local_map schema and the verifiers that judge its output on the author's side, because a gate written by the party that wrote the thing under test is not a gate. This file exists so the producer has something concrete to emit and so the author has something concrete to reject; it is not the authority. A local_map is a NAVIGATIONAL RE-INDEXING of evidence a certificate already carries — it must add no knowledge of its own. Round 1 admits provenance kind 'certificate_inherited' only; on-board self-cartography is a strictly stronger claim and gets its own round.

provenance.description: Where the map's knowledge came from. Round 1 is certificate-inherited, so the certificate is the authority and this map is derived from it mechanically.

kind.description: Deliberately a const, not an enum. A later kind ('self_cartography', 'search_byproduct') is a different claim and must arrive with its own schema version, so that a round-1 verifier cannot silently accept round-3 evidence.

status.description: A map may not descend from a failed certification.

profile.description: A conformance certificate is a self-test against synthetic fixtures; it says nothing about this device.

tier.description: Carried so a gate can refuse a routing-class map on a non-sacrificial board without having to know class names.

class_entry_count.description: Entries the frozen DB names for this class. Deliberately recorded ALONGSIDE attested_count so the gap is visible in the artifact: the class is larger than what has been certified, and only the certified part is writable.

universe.description: The complete, exclusive set of addresses a mutation operator may write. Anything not here is out of bounds, including entries the frozen DB names but no specimen pair ever attested.

collateral.description: Bit changes that are consequences of a legitimate write rather than violations. Carried in the map because the diff gate must distinguish them, and the rule must come from the certificate's own exclusion record rather than from a gate's private knowledge.

scope.description: An ECC change in a frame the candidate did not touch is a violation, not collateral. Stating the scope in the artifact stops a gate from widening it to 'any frame' for convenience.

index.description: The re-indexing itself, and the only part of the map that is not a restatement of the certificate. Certificates are ordered per feature for auditing; a mutation operator needs the inverse. Whether this indexing measurably helps navigation IS Claim B.

by_far.description: FAR -> the writable addresses inside that frame. Lets an operator (and the diff gate) know which frames a candidate touches, hence which ECC fields are legitimate collateral.

by_lut.description: LUT (feature prefix, e.g. 'CLBLL_L.SLICEL_X0.ALUT') -> its writable INIT bits, ordered by INIT index. This is the structural relation a map-guided operator can exploit and a blind one cannot: these bits are one truth table, not 64 unrelated bits.

repo_relative_path.description: Repo-relative, never absolute and never escaping upward. Absolute paths make a tree non-relocatable and describe a filesystem the verifier does not have.

address_key.description: Canonical 'FAR/word/bit'. A single string so the two indexes reference addresses rather than duplicating them, and so a mismatch is an exact-equality question.

expected_value.description: The polarity from the certificate: 0 for a '!'-negated segbit token, 1 otherwise. An operator that ignores polarity writes the wrong value for negated bits.

split.description: The ADDRESS-certification split, carried for provenance only. It is not a Claim B train/holdout split and must never be used as one.
